verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्युवाच।सोमदत्तसुतं पश्य युयुधानेन पातितम्। वितुद्यमानं विहगैर्बहुभिर्माधवान्तिके॥१॥
पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्तः शोमदत्तो जनार्दन। युयुधानं महेष्वासं गर्हयन्निव दृश्यते॥२॥
असौ हि भूरिश्रवसो माता शोकपरिप्लुता। आश्वासयति भर्तारं सोमदत्तमनिन्दिता॥३॥
verses.english: There the mother of Bhurishravas that faultless lady, beside herself with grief, is addressing her lord Somadatta, saying,-By good luck, O king, you do not witness this terrible destruction of the Bharatas, this extermination of the Kurus, this sight resembling the spectacles occurring at the end of a cycle.

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या नैनं महाराज दारुणं भरतक्षयम्। कुरुसङ्क्रन्दनं घोरं युगान्तमनुपश्यसि॥४॥
दिष्ट्या यूपध्वजं पुत्रं वीरं भूरिसहस्रदम्। अनेकक्रतुयज्वानं निहतं नानुपश्यसि॥५॥
verses.english: By good luck, you do not see your heroic, son, who bore the device of the sacrificial stake on his banner and who celebrated numberless sacrifices with profuse presents to all, killed on the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या स्नुषाणामाक्रन्दे घोरं विलपितं बहु। न शृणोषि महाराज सारसीनामिवार्णवे॥६॥
verses.english: By good luck, you do not hear those dreadful wails of woe uttered amidst this destruction by your daughter-in-law like the screams of a fight of cranes of the sea.

verses.sanskrit: एकवस्त्रार्धसंवीताः प्रकीर्णाः सितमूर्धजाः। स्नुषास्ते परिधावन्ति हतापत्या हतेश्वराः॥७॥
verses.english: Your daughters-in-law, deprived of both husbands and sons, are running about, each clad in a single piece of cloth and each with her clad in a single piece of cloth and each with her black hairs all disheveled.

verses.sanskrit: श्वापदैर्भक्ष्यमाणं त्वमहो दिष्ट्या न पश्यसि। छिन्नबाहुं नरव्याघ्रमर्जुनेन निपातितम्॥८॥
verses.english: By good luck, you do not see to-day your son, that foremost of men, deprived of one of his arms, killed by Arjuna, and now being devoured by beasts of prey.

verses.sanskrit: शलं विनिहतं सङ्ख्ये भूरिश्रवसमेव च। स्नुषाश्च विविधाः सर्वा दिष्ट्या नाद्येह पश्यसि॥९॥
दिष्ट्या तत्काञ्चनं छत्रं यूपकेतोर्महात्मनः। विनीकीर्णं रथोपस्थे सौमदत्तेर्न पश्यसि॥१०॥
अमूस्तु भूरिश्रवसो भार्याः सात्यकिना हतम्। परिवार्यानुशोचन्ति भर्तारमसितेक्षणाः॥११॥
verses.english: There the black-eyed wives of Bhurishravas are bewailing piteously surrounding their lord killed by Satyaki.

verses.sanskrit: एता विलप्य करुणं भर्तृशोकेन कर्शिताः। पतन्त्यभिमुखा भूमौ कृपणं बत केशव॥१२॥
बीभत्सुरतिबीभत्सं कर्मेदमकरोत्कथम्। प्रमत्तस्य यदच्छैत्सीद्बाहुं शूरस्य यज्वनः॥१३॥
ततः पापतरं कर्म कृतवानपि सात्यकिः। यस्मात्प्रायोपविष्टस्य प्राहार्षीत्संशितात्मनः॥१४॥
एको द्वाभ्यां हतः शेते त्वमधर्मेण धार्मिक। किन्नु वक्ष्यति वै सत्सु गोष्ठीषु च सभासु च॥१५॥
verses.english: Alas, O righteous one, you are lying on the ground, killed unfairly by two foes. Thus, O Madhava, those wives of Bhurishravas are crying aloud in sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: अपुण्यमयशस्यं च कर्मेदं सात्यकिः स्वयम्। इति यूपध्वजस्यैताः स्त्रियः क्रोशन्ति माधव॥१६॥
verses.english: There, those wives of that warrior, all having slender waists, are placing upon their laps the cut off arm of their husband and weeping bitterly. Here is that arm which used to attack the girdles, grind the deep bosoms and touch the navel, the thighs, and the hips, of fair ladies, and loosen the ties of the drawers worn by them.

verses.sanskrit: भार्या यूपध्वजस्यैषा करसम्मितमध्यमा। कृत्वोत्सङ्गे भुजं भर्तुः कृपणं परिदेवति॥१७॥
अयं स हन्ता शूराणां मित्राणामभयप्रदः। प्रदाता गोसहस्राणां क्षत्रियान्तकरः करः॥१८॥
अयं स रसनोत्कर्षी पीनस्तनविमर्दनः। नाभ्यूरुजघनस्पर्शी नीवीविस्रंसनः करः॥१९॥
वासुदेवस्य सान्निध्ये पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। युध्यतः समरेऽन्येन प्रमत्तस्य निपातितः॥२०॥
किन्नु वक्ष्यसि संसत्सु कथासु च जनार्दन। अर्जुनस्य महत्कर्म स्वयं वा स किरीटभृत्॥२१॥
इत्येवं गर्हयित्वैषा तूष्णीमास्ते वराङ्गना। तामेतामनुशोचन्ति सपत्न्यः स्वामिव स्नुषाम्॥२२॥
verses.english: How will you, O Janarddana, describe this great fear of Arjuna while speaking of it in the midst of assemblies. What also will the diadem-decked Arjuna himself say of it?-Censuring you in this way, that best of ladies nas stopped at last. The co-wives of that lady are lamenting piteously with her as if she wee their daughter-in-law.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्बलवान्सत्यविक्रमः। निहतः सहदेवेन भागिनेयेन मातुलः॥२३॥
verses.english: There the powerful Shakuni, the king of the Gandharas, having irresistible prowess, has been killed by Sahadeva, the maternal uncle by the sister's son.

verses.sanskrit: यः पुरा हेमदण्डाभ्यां व्यजनाभ्यां स्म वीज्यते। स एष पक्षिभिः पक्षैः शयान उपवीज्यते॥२४॥
verses.english: Formerly, he used to be fanned with a two gold-handed fans. Alas, now, his boy lunging on the ground is being fanned by birds with their wings.

verses.sanskrit: यः स्वरूपाणि कुरुते शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। तस्य मायाविनो माया दग्धाः पाण्डवतेजसा॥२५॥
verses.english: He used to assume hundreds and thousands of forms. All the illusions, however, of that man possessed of great illusory powers, have been burnt by the energy of the son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: मायया निकृतिप्रज्ञो जितवान्यो युधिष्ठिरम्। सभायां विपुलं राज्यं स पुनर्जीवितं जितः॥२६॥
शकुन्ताः शकुनिं कृष्ण समन्तात्पर्युपासते। कैतवं मम पुत्राणां विनाशायोपशिक्षितम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Look, O Krishna, a number of birds is not sitting around Shakuni. An expert in dice, alas, he had also mastered the means for the destruction of my sons.

verses.sanskrit: एतेनैतन्महद्वैरं प्रसक्तं पाण्डवैः सह। वधाय मम पुत्राणामात्मनः सगणस्य च॥२८॥
verses.english: This fire of hostility with the Pandavas had been lighted by Shakuni, for the destruction of my children as also of himself and his followers ar relatives.

verses.sanskrit: यथैव मम पुत्राणां लोकाः शस्त्रजिताः प्रभो। एवमस्यापि दुर्बुद्धेर्लोकाः शस्त्रेण वै जिताः॥२९॥
verses.english: Like those gained by my sons, O powerful one, by the use of arms, this man too, however wicked-souled, has obtained many blissful regions by the use of weapons.

verses.sanskrit: कथं च नायं तत्रापि पुत्रान्मे भ्रातृभिः सह। विरोधयेदृजुप्रज्ञाननृजुर्मधुसूदन॥३०॥
verses.english: My fear, O destroyer of Madhu, is that wily man may not create dissensions even there between my children all of whom are simple and confiding.
